clue.text: This could cause a major shake-up in Hollywood

definitions.text: This could cause a major shake-up in Hollywood

parts.words: This could cause a major shake-up in Hollywood
parts.note: a shake-up here is an earthquake, and the geological fracture running through California threatens the film capital

explanation.surface: Something is set to cause a big upheaval among the film studios.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shake-up' reads as a corporate reshuffle at the studios, but it is a literal earthquake: the great Californian fault line lies near Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian fault line is the source of major earthquakes, the literal shake-ups of Los Angeles.

clue.text: One's showing ice — ie must have this!

definitions.text: One's showing ice — ie must have this!

parts.words: One's showing ice — ie must have this!
parts.note: someone icy in manner shows a lack of warmth; and the word ice is the letters I and E with C, the cold abbreviation, put at its heart

explanation.surface: A remark about someone displaying an icy manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: an icy person shows a frosty, unfeeling nature, and the word 'ice' is 'ie' with C (cold) at its centre, so 'ie' must be cold at heart to become it.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing ice in one's manner means lacking warmth or feeling, an unfeeling quality of character.

clue.text: Minor deviation — one sounds stifled manifesting repressed anger

indicators.note: stifled means smothered or held inside, so the word one is enclosed within the other pieces

parts.note: a minor part is a bit part
a slip is a small deviation or error
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small mistake makes someone go quiet, showing suppressed fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' only links, adding to the picture of muffled noise; the definition is the past-tense idiom for holding back an angry retort.
explanation.definitionFit: To have held back an angry remark by clamping the mouth shut is an idiom for suppressing rage.

clue.text: State of America was on Charles's mind

definitions.meaning: a US state in the South, capital Atlanta
the song '... on My Mind' was famously recorded by Ray Charles

explanation.definitionFit: It is a southern US state, and the title subject of Ray Charles's hit song about it being on his mind.

clue.text: Party man must agree to avoid some left- and rightwingers

indicators.text: to avoid some left- and rightwingers
indicators.note: dropping some letters from the left and right ends of the phrase must agree leaves the run inside

explanation.surface: A party member has to agree in order to steer clear of both political extremes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' and 'left- and rightwingers' suggest politics; the indicator means trimming letters from each end of 'must agree', leaving the middle run.
explanation.definitionFit: A man attending an all-male party before his wedding is the guest of honour at such a do.

clue.text: No offence — laddie's drunk non-alcoholic drink

indicators.note: drunk suggests being jumbled about, so the letters of no offence laddie are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone apologises to a young man who is drunk and offers him a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' sits ironically beside 'non-alcoholic'; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A caffeine-free beverage brewed from roasted roots of a common weed contains no alcohol.

clue.text: Party at home gets nerveracking aound 4 with lots of workers needed

parts.note: the Labour Party is a major British political party
in means at home

indicators.note: a misprint of around, telling us one piece encloses the other

parts.note: something tense is nerve-racking
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A political party's homecoming turns stressful, requiring a big workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aound' is printed so and means 'around'. The Labour Party is one of Britain's two main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Work needing many hands rather than machines is described as demanding much human effort.

clue.text: Plant with flower seen by old yards (lots of them!)

parts.note: a flower here is something that flows, a river: the Cam flows through Cambridge
a mile is 1,760 yards

explanation.surface: A plant with a bloom growing beside an ancient garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river (it flows): the Cam runs through Cambridge in England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a daisy-like herb used to make a soothing tea, so a plant.

clue.text: A mother wants to be in the fashion, without exception

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the word for fashion

parts.note: the ton is an old word for high fashion or fashionable society
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A mum longs to be trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ton' is an old word for high society or the height of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone, every single person, as in an idiom saying they acted unanimously.

clue.text: Fern or aromatic plant attracting ducks

parts.note: nard, or spikenard, is an aromatic plant
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A fern or a scented herb draws waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' are noughts (a duck is a zero in cricket), so OO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian aquatic plant of the clover-leafed fern family whose spores were eaten by Aboriginal people.

clue.text: Dance in the capital with party taking place

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
a do is a party
on means happening, as in 'the show is on'

explanation.surface: A dance in the capital city during a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively old Provençal folk dance in duple time, popular in the 17th century.

clue.text: Hit unconvincingly, getting boundary

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to nick the ball off the side of the bat

explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer nicks the ball off the bat's side, and the noun also means a border or margin.

clue.text: Like certain writing from Italy, prose that's fancy

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters of Italy and prose are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ornate prose from Italy suggests a particular literary style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's fancy' signals an anagram of ITALY PROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature written in the form of letters, like a novel told through correspondence.

clue.text: Nicking material from the drapery?

explanation.surface: Stealing fabric from a draper's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for pocketing money dishonestly, and the term for cloth used to make trousers.

clue.text: Hot month when it should be cold? Bother!

parts.words: month when it should be cold?
parts.note: February is a winter month in Britain
to bother is to rile or irritate

explanation.surface: A warm month in winter is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: FEB is short for February, a winter month in the northern hemisphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish, from the Latin for fever, so running a high temperature.

clue.text: Record something locking road around that industrial city

indicators.note: around means the traffic piece goes round the record word

parts.note: a traffic cone closes off a road
a log is a record

explanation.surface: A record of a road being closed around an industrial city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something locking road' is a traffic cone, used to close off a lane.
explanation.definitionFit: A major industrial city on the Rhine in Germany.

clue.text: Plant not going anywhere, having little energy

parts.note: static means stationary
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A plant stays still with little vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea lavender, a plant often dried for flower arrangements.

clue.text: As the stoop gets worse, they can offer manipulation

indicators.note: a worsening stoop is a deformed one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: As someone's posture deteriorates, practitioners can help with treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets worse' signals an anagram of AS THE STOOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Practitioners who treat the body by manipulating bones and muscles.

clue.text: Fly on at maximum speed

parts.note: c is the speed of light, the universe's maximum speed
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: An insect flying flat out.
explanation.walkthrough: C (speed of light) comes before LEG, the cricket on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A horsefly, a biting insect, in older and regional usage.

clue.text: Girl wearing hat for "Sir"

indicators.note: a head wears the hat, so the girl's name goes inside the headgear

parts.note: a beret is a hat
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl puts on a hat for a knighted gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight who led men under his own banner, entitled to be called Sir.

clue.text: Authors? A US sequence includes him, possibly

definitions.text: Authors? A US sequence includes him, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of authors can be rearranged into a US sequence plus another name

explanation.surface: Among American authors, he might be included.
explanation.walkthrough: AUTHORS rearranged is A, U, S in sequence plus THOR, which rearranges to the American novelist Philip's surname: the whole clue defines him as one of the US authors.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip, the American novelist, is one of the US authors.

clue.text: At the game, can you see the ________ his whistle? Rubbish!

definitions.text: At the game, can you see the ________ his whistle?
definitions.meaning: split as two words the gap reads referee then use, filling the sentence

explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is waste matter, and split in two the letters fill the blank with the referee using his whistle.

clue.text: Private firm entertaining large group

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the firm piece holds the large piece inside

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A private company hosting a big party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier but is an adjective meaning secret or hidden away.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means secret or hidden, kept private.

clue.text: Tory minister to provide safeguard

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
to minister is to serve

explanation.surface: A Conservative minister promises protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' is a verb here (to minister to = serve), not a government official.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve or protect something from harm or waste.
